heading: INT. APOTHECARY SHOP, MARKET TOWN - 1740 - EVENING

units.text: INT. APOTHECARY SHOP, MARKET TOWN - 1740 - EVENING
Low beams.
Shelves of blue glass jars with handwritten labels.
A mortar and pestle, a scale, a bundle of dried lavender hung from a rafter.
A coal stove ticks in the corner.
APOTHECARY BARNABAS ADEYEMI-HOLLOWAY (50s, ink-stained apron, round spectacles) is grinding something in a bowl.
His movements are slow and deliberate.
His apprentice, KEZIAH OSEI-LINDQVIST (16, linen cap, sleeves rolled to the elbow), sorts herbs into drawers, humming under her breath.
In the corner, on a stool by the stove, sits GIDEON PELL-ADEBOYE (60s, patched coat, a clay pipe unlit in his teeth), a regular who has said nothing in an hour and will say nothing more.
The shop bell rings.
A WOMAN in a traveling cloak enters, rain on her shoulders.
She is ISOLDE FAIRCHILD-ADEBAYO (30s, pale, careful, a worn leather satchel), and she carries herself like someone who has practiced being unremarkable.
She shakes out her cloak, hangs it on a peg.
He watches her without seeming to.
She smiles.
He smiles back.
Good evening, sir.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: Madam. A foul night.
units.name: BARNABAS

units.text: I was told you stock rue.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: We do. For what complaint?
units.name: BARNABAS

units.text: A friend's.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: He sets down the pestle and goes to the shelf.
She follows him with her eyes.
She steps closer to the counter, and from the satchel her hand slips something small and flat, which she lays on the wood.
Keziah stops humming.
Barnabas returns with a jar.
He sets it down.
Sees the thing on the counter.
His face does not change, but his hand does, closing over the jar's lid as if to keep it from spilling.
Where did you come by this?
units.name: BARNABAS

units.text: Does it matter?
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: It is a seal ring, silver, with an unfamiliar crest.
He picks it up.
Turns it over.
Keziah watches his thumb stroke the inside of the band.
Keziah. Lock the door.
units.name: BARNABAS

units.text: She does.
The bolt falls with a sound like a dropped coin.
I was told you'd know the crest.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: I know it.
units.name: BARNABAS

units.text: Then you know why I've come.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: He looks at Keziah.
At the stove.
At the ring in his palm.
He says nothing for a long time.
Sit, madam.
units.name: BARNABAS

units.text: She sits.
The coal ticks.
Rain presses on the window.
